findings.issue: Here αὐτίκα γοῦν introduces an illustrative case. The temporal rendering makes the Egyptian leaders' conduct immediate, although the passage supplies no corresponding temporal relationship.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the opening with “For example,” and document the exemplificatory use of αὐτίκα γοῦν. The revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: πλὴν τὰ ἀλλήλων γελᾶτε· τὰ γὰρ ἴδια ὑπὸ συνηθείας κακῆς εἰς ἀπάτην ἀχθέντες οὐ βλέπετε.
findings.english_quote: Yet you laugh at one another’s practices; but your own you do not see, because evil custom has led you into deception.
findings.issue: The draft substitutes an adversative “but” for the explanatory γάρ. The Greek explains their reciprocal ridicule by their failure to perceive their own practices; the draft's “because” instead expresses only the relationship between bad custom and deception.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Yet you laugh at one another’s practices, for you do not see your own, having been led into deception by evil custom.” Submit the revised sentence for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὅτι δὲ ὄντως ὀρθῶς καταγελᾶτε τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, σύνφημι
findings.english_quote: I agree that you rightly ridicule the Egyptians
findings.issue: The explicit affirmation ὄντως is not represented. “Rightly” translates ὀρθῶς, while “I agree” translates σύνφημι; neither separately preserves the additional emphasis that their ridicule really is justified.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “I agree that you do indeed rightly ridicule the Egyptians.” Review the revised wording afresh.

findings.source_quote: οἱ μὲν γὰρ ὑμῶν κρόμμυον ὑπονοήσαντες εἶναι τὸ θεῖον καὶ γαστρὸς πνεύματα σέβοντες πολεμοῦσιν
findings.english_quote: Some of you, having supposed the divine to be an onion and venerating winds from a belly, wage war
findings.issue: The draft attaches both participles to the same worshiping group without disclosing the material alternative that καί coordinates two groups: those who suppose the divine to be an onion and those who venerate abdominal winds. The shared article and nominative participles make the draft's construction defensible, but the ensuing description of each group preferring one object and criticizing others supports the rival-group construal. This is interpretive ambiguity, not source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note preserving the alternative: “Some among you—the ones supposing the divine to be an onion and the ones venerating winds from a belly—wage war.” Explain that the main text follows the shared-subject construction, while the context supports distributing the participles between rival groups. Do not supply an explicit object for “wage war” as though it were printed. The amended passage and note require fresh review.
